about.title: About Quran.us.kg App
about.description: Quran.us.kg is an open-source Quran app built to offer an ideal listening experience across all platforms. The app is built using modern web technologies to ensure:
about.feature.responsive: Responsive design for all screen sizes
about.feature.providers: Recitations from multiple providers, with the source shown for each reciter
about.mission: The app aims to provide an accessible and permanent source for the Holy Quran while maintaining the highest technical and design standards.
about.providers.title: Multiple recitation providers
about.providers.description1: The app brings recitations together from several independent providers, including MP3Quran, Itqan, Qurani.ai and Quran Foundation. Every reciter row names its source, and you can choose which sources are enabled in Settings.
about.providers.description2: These providers are independent third-party services, not part of the app. Audio quality, timing data and download support can differ between them, and the app shows what each source supports.
about.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
about.faq.a1: Yes. The app is free and open source, and listening needs no account.
about.faq.a2: Yes. You can download surahs from sources that allow downloads and listen without a connection.
about.faq.q3: Where do the recitations come from?
about.faq.a3: Recitations come from several sources including MP3Quran, Itqan, Qurani.ai and Quran Foundation. Each reciter row names its source.
about.faq.a4: The interface is available in Arabic, English and German, and several recitation riwayat are supported.
privacy.title: Open Tarteel Privacy Policy
privacy.section1.title: Your Privacy Matters to Us
privacy.section1.body: At Quran.us.kg, we take your privacy seriously. This policy outlines our approach to privacy and data collection in the app.
privacy.section2.title: What Information Do We Collect?
privacy.section2.body: The Quran.us.kg app does not collect any personal information or other user data. The app runs entirely offline, and no data is transmitted from your device.
privacy.section3.title: Why Don’t We Collect Data?
privacy.section3.point1: To provide a seamless offline experience
privacy.section3.point2: No need for analytics or tracking data
privacy.section4.title: We Respect Your Children’s Privacy
privacy.section4.body: Quran.us.kg is designed for children aged 6 and up who can read Arabic. We are committed to protecting children's privacy. Since our app collects no data, children’s information is entirely safe.
privacy.section5.title: Keeping Your Data Secure
privacy.section5.body: As we collect no data, there is no personal information to protect. However, we continue to prioritize app security by regularly monitoring for potential vulnerabilities.
privacy.section6.title: Your Privacy Rights
privacy.section6.body: Since no personal data is collected, there is no need for deletion requests or managing personal information within the app.
privacy.section7.title: Third-Party Services
privacy.section7.body: Quran.us.kg does not use any third-party services for analytics, tracking, or data collection. The app works entirely on your device without sending any information externally.

privacy.section8.body: If you have any questions about this policy, feel free to contact us at:

account.title: Account
account.description: Optional. Link your devices into a ring and your favourites and settings follow you between them.
account.createNote: A ring is a key generated here and kept in this browser — no username, no password. Add another device now if you want the ring and its favourites to outlive this one.
account.privacyNote: What a ring syncs — favourites, settings and device names — is kept on a public sync relay. It is signed, so only your devices can change it, but it is not encrypted: anyone who knows the ring’s public key can read it.
account.joinNote: Scan a code from a device already in the ring, and this device copies the key.
account.manualNote: For devices without a camera: copy the code from the other device and paste it here.
account.manualInvalid: That code is not valid, or it has expired
account.shareTitle: Add a device to the ring
account.shareNote: The code carries a one-time key, not the ring key. It expires in two minutes and is burned as soon as a device reads it.
account.shareWarning: For those two minutes the code is your ring: anyone who scans or copies it joins with full access. Show it only to your own devices.
account.scanHint: Point the camera at the pairing code
account.linkedHere: This device is now in the ring
account.linkedOther: A new device was added to the ring
account.linkedHint: The ring’s devices are listed below, and favourites and settings now sync on their own.
account.codeTimeout: The pairing code did not arrive. Check your connection and try again.
account.cameraBlockedTitle: The browser is blocking the camera
account.cameraBlockedNote: Allow the camera for this site in the browser settings, then try again.
account.cameraNoDeviceNote: Copy the code from the other device and paste it here; the result is the same.
account.cameraBusyNote: Another app is using it. Close that app and try again, or paste the code instead.
account.cameraSecureNote: The camera only works over https or localhost. Paste the code instead.
account.codeFailed: Could not create a pairing code
account.devicesNote: Every device in this ring holds the same key. Signing one out only affects that device; it does not revoke the key.
account.signOutSafe: Your other devices stay signed in. This browser forgets the key and will need a new pairing code.
account.signOutLast: This is the only device in the ring. Signing out here erases the key from this browser, and there is no password to bring it back — the ring and every favourite in it become unrecoverable. Add another device first, or keep this one.
privacy.ring.title: The account ring (optional)
privacy.ring.body: Listening needs no account. If you create a ring to sync your devices, the following applies:
privacy.ring.point1: Your favourites, the synced settings (appearance, sources, sort order, spectrum and speed) and the names of your devices are stored on Open Tarteel’s public sync relay. They are signed, so only a device holding the ring key can change them, but they are not encrypted: anyone who knows the ring’s public key can read them.
privacy.ring.point2: The ring key leaves your devices only inside a pairing code. For its two minutes a pairing code is the ring: whoever scans or copies it in that time joins with full access. It is deleted from the relay as soon as a device reads it.
privacy.ring.point3: Signing out erases the key from that browser only. There is no password and no recovery: if the last device signs out, the ring cannot be opened again.
